questions.q: Under decision D14, which file is the append-only queue journal, and who is the only writer of it?
questions.key: `.guilda/queue/journal.jsonl`; only the orchestrator writes it (the Architect until the orchestrator exists).

questions.q: Under decision D8, at which tier can a re-review of a small fix run, and what counts as small?
questions.key: journeyman; at most about 50 changed lines, no risk area, no shared code.

questions.q: Under decision D10, what does the ARC4 fallback do if the model of a tier is not available?
questions.key: Use one tier higher, and tell the user. (The spec changed from 'lower' to 'higher'.)

questions.q: Which plan task owns decision D14?
Which briefs cite decision D24 on their `Uses:` line?
Does brief T5 still match decision D17 as it is now in the spec? Answer yes or no, with the reason.
questions.key: No. T5 says one append-only JSONL mailbox file for each code in `.guilda/bus/`; D17 now says one SQLite table in `.guilda/bus.db` for all codes.

questions.q: Does brief T4 still match decision D10 as it is now in the spec? Answer yes or no, with the reason.
questions.key: Yes. T4 uses only the D10 rule that each dispatch states the reply language; that rule did not change (only the ARC4 fallback changed).

questions.q: Under decision D13, after how many days does Claude Code delete a subagent transcript by default?
Under decision D20, which marker and which label format does each row of an agent from outside the conversation have?
Does brief T6 still match decision D24 as it is now in the spec? Answer yes or no, with the reason.
questions.key: No. T6 says `status` is an internal script and the user sees the state only in the panel; D24 now says `status` stays a user command that the user types.

review.q: The spec changed after the briefs were written. Check each of the 6 briefs in docs/superpowers/briefs/ against the decisions it cites, as the spec is now. For each brief, say if a spec change affects it (the brief no longer matches a decision that it cites) and why. Also report any problem with a `Uses:` line.
review.end: End your reply with one line `AFFECTED: <brief IDs, comma separated>` that lists only the briefs whose text no longer matches the spec.
review.key: AFFECTED: T1, T3, T5, T6. T4 cites the changed D10 but still matches. T2 cites an unknown ID D99 (a Uses problem, not a mismatch).

grading: Strict. The grader reads the ANSWER line (the AFFECTED line for the review). An answer is correct only if it matches every pattern in `all` and no pattern in `none` (case-insensitive). A run with no ANSWER line, a timeout or an error is wrong. A human check confirms each automatic grade.
